Subject: Q3 launch — pricing & guaranteed usage schedule

Hi Karthik,

Were locking down vendor commitments for a July launch and I wanted to surface a couple of requirements so we can compare economics and operational exposure across vendors. Horizons product launches are heavily front-loaded (week-of-launch spikes ~4-6x baseline for 10 days), then settle into a seasonally-weighted baseline that grows over the next 6–9 months.

Key asks:
- A per-token hosted API pricing schedule with native monthly commit tiers (were evaluating both hard commits and step-up month-over-month schedules).
- True-up policy and mid-month burst/overage protections for launch spikes. Do you offer a burst buffer or dynamic burst credits on top of a committed baseline?
- Any recommended smoothing/seasonality clauses (we prefer predictable billing).
- Contract length (12/24/36 mo) and any ramp-based discounts.

Attached is a short RFP with our expected daily distribution (sample usage curve) and compliance questions. Can you send a proposed monthly-commit calendar and an example invoice cadence? Wed like a first pass by EOD today if possible — leadership wants a shortlist before our procurement sync next week.

Thanks,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear brief and the RFP, helpful. High-level proposal below; I attached a draft commit schedule (proposed-commit-schedule.xlsx) with the numbers so your procurement team can model cashflow.

Summary options (hosted API, per-token basis):
1) Conservative monthly commit (12m contract): baseline tiers with small monthly step-ups. E.g., Month 0 pilot 500k tokens, Month 1 = 1.5M, Month 2 = 3M, Month 3+ = 5M steady. Discount progression: 10% @ 1M+, 18% @ 3M+, 25% @ 5M+.
2) Aggressive ramp (24m): deeper up-front discount for larger commit guarantees; includes quarterly true-up and a 6-day burst buffer (temporary overage protection up to 3x baseline for launch window) we can provision as reserved burst capacity.

Key policies:
- True-up: monthly reconciliation; overages billed at the committed tier rate (not penalized at list), with option to convert overage to a higher committed tier for subsequent months.
- Burst buffer: reserved burst pool that bills at a reduced overage rate if you keep within agreed burst days for a given quarter. We can structure usage credits to cover the 10-day launch period.
- Seasonality smoothing: apply a rolling 3-month average to avoid single-month spikes causing immediate tier jumps; optional smoothing clause on 12m deals.

Operational notes: to size the right tier we need: 1) expected peak qps and token/response distribution, 2) ratio of chat vs. single-shot embeddings (affects token mix). Marcus, can you add a brief note on throughput and how caching/kv-prefixing will change the effective token bill?

Can we do a 30-minute call today at 3pm PT to walk the numbers? If that works, Ill have a redlineable term sheet ready for your procurement.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-commit-schedule.xlsx (xlsx)

Priya — quick technical add from my side to make sure the economics map to your traffic profile.

A few practical levers we recommend:
- Prefix/KV caching: if you have repeated prompts or system messages we can reduce billable tokens by ~12–20% for the same perceived latency. Weve seen this across past launches where templated flows dominate peak traffic.
- Quantization profile: running an 8-bit quantized variant for high-throughput endpoints reduces cost and improves variance, but wed validate model output quality against your eval set first. Its compatible with a committed tier, and we can publish a separate microtier price for quantized inference.
- Burst sizing: for a 6–10 day launch spike at 4–6x baseline, recommend reserving a burst pool equal to ~2x baseline (keeps cost predictable) and allowing automatic fallback to pay-as-you-go once burst credits exhaust. That approach buys you capacity without overcommitting monthly spend.

Concrete ramp suggestion (aligned with Karthiks sheets):
- Month 0 (pilot): 500k tokens (validation)
- Month 1 (soft launch): 1.5M tokens, include 1x burst credits for the launch week
- Month 2 (scale): 3M tokens, increase burst pool to 1.5x baseline
- Month 3+: target steady commit 5M tokens/month (apply 3-month smoothing for invoice tiering)

Invoice cadence: monthly with end-of-month true-up and an itemized burst line. We can also offer quarterly invoicing for finance teams that prefer it; pricing slightly improved for quarterly prepay.

If you can share a short sample of token distribution (per request percentiles), Ill run a quick cost simulator and send a comparison of "committed + burst" vs. pure pay-as-you-go.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
